questions.q: In the number 15.67, what is the place value of the digit 6?
questions.a: The place value is the tenths place (or 0.6). A student who answers "tens" is confusing the tenths place (to the right of the decimal) with the tens place (to the left of the decimal).

questions.q: Why is the digit 3 in 0.03 worth less than the digit 3 in 0.3?
questions.a: The digit 3 in 0.3 is in the tenths place (3/10), while the 3 in 0.03 is in the hundredths place (3/100). A student who says "because it is on the right" is missing the specific fractional value of each position.

questions.q: The value is 8/100. A student who writes 8/10 or 8/1000 has failed to count the positions correctly from the decimal point (tenths, hundredths, thousandths).
questions.a:
The value of the digit 8 in the number 24.582 is 8/100. This is because the 8 is in the hundredths place, meaning it represents eight parts out of one hundred.

A wrong answer reveals that the student likely confuses the place value positions of decimals, such as misidentifying the hundredths place as the tenths (8/10) or the thousandths (8/1000) place. It may also indicate a failure to understand that the denominator of a decimal fraction is determined by the digit's distance from the decimal point.

questions.q: If you move a digit one place to the right in a decimal number, how does its value change?
questions.a: Its value becomes 1/10th of its previous value. Answering "it gets smaller" is too vague; the student must understand the specific power-of-ten relationship between adjacent decimal places.

questions.q: Is 0.50 greater than, less than, or equal to 0.5? Justify your answer using place value.
questions.a: They are equal because 0.5 is 5/10, and 0.50 is 50/100, which simplifies to 5/10. A student who claims 0.50 is larger is mistakenly treating the decimal part like a whole number (thinking 50 is bigger than 5).

questions.q: Create a decimal number where the digit 4 has a value of 0.004 and the digit 7 has a value of 70.
questions.a: A correct answer is 70.004 or 72.404 (as long as 4 is in the thousandths place and 7 is in the tens place). An incorrect answer reveals the student cannot correctly map the digit to its required fractional or whole-number position.
